top_stories.title: Polymarket Launches Protocol V2: Ground-Up Rebuild
points: Polymarket rebuilt its entire prediction market system (a platform where users bet on outcomes of real-world events) from scratch, replacing the 2019 Gnosis Conditional Tokens Framework.
New architecture consolidates fragmented contract layers into a single ERC1155 positions contract, one pUSD collateral token, one exchange, and one router.
Settlement (the mechanism determining winners and paying out profits) is now faster, reducing wait times for payouts after events resolve.
An OracleAggregator with pluggable resolution modules connects to UMA, Chainlink, and future oracle sources (services that feed real-world data on-chain) for flexible market resolution.
First-class multi-chain bridging support for positions, collateral, and resolutions lays groundwork for expansion without disrupting existing integrations.
Launches with four market types — Binary, Atomic Neg-risk, Incremental Neg-risk, and Combinatorial — upgradeable via governance.
Rebuild targets higher concurrent trading volume and lower transaction costs, addressing technical debt from years on the old system.

unique_angles.point: Specifies the new protocol replaces the 2019 Gnosis Conditional Tokens Framework and details the exact consolidated contract structure and four launch market types.
Frames the rebuild as addressing years of accumulated technical debt and preparing for mainstream adoption of crypto derivatives.

items.title: FinCEN Withdraws 2023 Crypto Mixing Regulation
points: FinCEN withdrew its 2023 proposal that would have designated international crypto mixing (combining funds from multiple sources to obscure transaction trails) a 'primary money laundering concern' under Section 311.
Also abandoned a 2020 proposal requiring banks and money services to verify identities and keep records on self-hosted wallet transactions above $3,000.
Decision cited concerns that broad definitions would chill legitimate privacy use, referencing a July 2025 President's Working Group report acknowledging lawful privacy use of mixers.
FinCEN will continue monitoring mixers for illicit use but says existing obligations remain unchanged since neither proposal was finalized.

items.title: Stripe Taps Privy Founder for Stablecoin Platform
points: Stripe appointed Privy founder Henri Stern to lead a stablecoin developer platform.
Platform integrates Bridge, Privy, Tempo, and Open USD to treat fiat and crypto as interoperable layers.

items.title: Chainalysis AI Traces $387M Bitget Hack to North Korea
points: Chainalysis attributed the $387M Bitget breach to North Korean actors using custom AI tools that compressed bridge reconciliation analysis from over 20 hours to under 10 minutes.
The attribution pushes North Korea's (DPRK) 2026 crypto theft total past $1 billion.
Within 3 hours, attackers dispersed funds across Ethereum (49.7%), XRP (40.8%), Zcash (7.6%), and Tron (1.8%) in 23 transfers.
Stolen XRP was routed through cross-chain liquidity protocols to convert to Bitcoin over roughly 36 hours.

items.title: Near Intents Recovers $3.8M Stolen Funds in 48 Hours
points: Near Intents recovered the full $3.8M stolen within 48 hours after identifying the attacker on-chain and issuing a return deadline with an implicit deanonymization threat.
This was the second major security incident on the platform in one week.
The exploit targeted a flaw in the Omni deposit/withdrawal layer's interaction with the main smart contract.
The attacker returned funds and posted an on-chain message acknowledging fault, urging use of bug bounties instead of exploits.

items.title: Zcash NU7 Upgrade Accelerates Block Times
points: Zcash activated the NU7 upgrade on public testnet, cutting target block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.
Three-confirmation finality time drops from 225 seconds to 75 seconds.
Block rewards split 40/60 between miners and a reserve for future mining rewards, with per-block rewards reduced to one-third to preserve ZEC's issuance schedule despite tripled block rate.
Upgrade retires Sprout, Zcash's original shielded payment protocol (a privacy feature hiding transaction details), requiring holders to migrate funds before the planned November 5 mainnet activation.
Both major node implementations (Zakura and Zebra) shipped compatible releases in early October, with an October 20 decision targeted for mainnet confirmation.

issues.subject: Polymarket Just Rebuilt Its Entire Protocol From the Ground Up

headlines: Polymarket completely rebuilt its prediction market protocol from scratch to improve scalability and user experience after operating on its previous infrastructure for years.
The new architecture introduces faster settlement times and reduced transaction costs, making it more competitive with traditional prediction market platforms.
Polymarket's protocol redesign suggests the platform is addressing technical debt and preparing for increased trading volume as crypto derivatives gain mainstream adoption.

sections.title: Polymarket's Complete Protocol Rebuild
points: 1. Polymarket migrated its entire prediction market system (a platform where users bet on the outcomes of real-world events) to a new protocol architecture designed from the ground up.
2. The rebuild focused on core infrastructure improvements including transaction speed, cost reduction, and platform reliability rather than feature additions.
3. Settlement processes (the mechanism that determines winners and pays out profits) now execute faster, reducing the time users wait to receive winnings after an event resolves.
4. The new protocol aims to handle higher concurrent trading volumes without performance degradation, addressing bottlenecks from the previous system.
